correctness.rationale: Independent calculation: for four ordered velocity times with successive gaps x,y,z, condition on the clock and use Gaussian pairings within unbroken intervals. The adjacent pairing factors and cancels from the connected moment. The two remaining pairings each require no refresh across the full span; subtracting the unconditional covariance products gives the connected moment 2 sigma^4 exp[-a1(x+z)](exp[-a2 y]-exp[-2 a1 y]), with a1=gamma+r and a2=2 gamma+r. It is strictly positive for positive gaps. Integration over the ordered time simplex, with the factor 24, proves strict displacement fourth cumulant at every positive time. After dividing by t the gap integrand acquires the factor (1-(x+y+z)/t)_+; dominated convergence gives 48 sigma^4/a1^2 times (1/a2-1/(2 a1)), exactly the claimed absolute rate. The covariance gives Var(X_t)/t -> 2 sigma^2/a1 and hence the claimed standardized rate. Differentiation gives the respective derivative signs 2 gamma^2-4 gamma r-3 r^2 and 2 gamma^2-r^2, establishing unique interior maxima. Repeating the endpoints of the connected moment and adding the two cross-pair products yields Cov(V_0^2,V_t^2)=2 sigma^4 exp[-a2 t]; the two lag slopes invert as stated. This route does not require interchanging derivatives and renewal limits.
residual_risks: No claim about a finite-time maximizing refresh rate, noisy inference, or non-Maxwellian resets; proof uses positive gamma, r and invariant Gaussian variance.

Comparing absolute and variance-normalized fourth-order transport also changes the predicted operating point substantially. This physical and inferential motivation is distinct from whether the formulas constitute a new contribution, which fails above.
